title: V. Since the world and its goods will soon perish, cling not; Christian wisdom dismisses the world — Cap. 6 close
pass_a_gloss: Hither looks Paul's warning (1 Corinthians 7:29, 30, 31) and David's (Psalm 49:4, 7, 12, 13, 15, 20, 21). but it belongs to Christian wisdom and felicity in this life to send a farewell to the world and its goods, so that after this life you may enjoy the eternal good. Since this world with all its goods will soon perish and cannot grant perpetual quiet and tranquillity to our mind, it stands as extreme madness and misery so to cling to it that by love of it you lose the true good; V.
pass_b_english: V. Since this world with all its goods will soon perish and cannot grant perpetual quiet and tranquillity to our mind, it is extreme madness and misery so to cling to it that by love of it you lose the true good; but it belongs to Christian wisdom and felicity in this life to send a farewell to the world and its goods, so that after this life you may enjoy the eternal good. Hither looks Paul's warning (1 Corinthians 7:29, 30, 31) and David's (Psalm 49:4, 7, 12, 13, 15, 20, 21).
source_text: V. Cum hic mundus cum omnibus bonis suis brevi interiturus, quietem ac tranquillitatem perpetuam animo nostro largiri nequeat, extrema vesania atque miseriae est, ei ita adhaerere, ut ejus amore verum bonum amittas; Christianae vero sapientiae & felicitatis est, in hac vita mundo ejusque bonis nuntium mittere, ut post hanc aeterno bono fruaris. Huc spectat monitio Pauli, 1.Cor. 7.29.30.31. & Davidis, Psal. 49.4.7.12.13.15.20.21.
